briefing.headline: Midterms reshape US politics as Wales faces policy crossroads
briefing.overview: US midterm results have shifted power to Democrats, prompting new strategies from both parties. In Wales, charities push for polluter taxes while a historic free school milk scheme faces possible closure.

stories.title: Trump reacts to midterm defeat
stories.what_happened: President Trump told 60 Minutes his immigration crackdown was "too tough" after Republicans lost heavily in the midterms. He said the defeat hurt him politically.
stories.why_it_matters: The story shows how election outcomes can influence executive policy choices, a key point in the AQA unit on the US President and elections. It also illustrates the link between public opinion and policy.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Trump’s base claim the crackdown protected jobs and security.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents say the policy was inhumane and cost voters support.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Republicans warn that softer immigration could weaken borders.

key_term.definition: US elections held halfway through a president's four‑year term, deciding control of Congress.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of how electoral defeat can force a president to adjust policy in an essay on executive responsiveness.

stories.title: Congress returns after Republican losses
stories.what_happened: After the midterms, Congress reconvened with Democrats holding majorities in both chambers. Republicans now face internal leadership battles and a looming shutdown deadline.
stories.why_it_matters: Illustrates the legislative branch’s role in checking the executive and the impact of party composition on law‑making, relevant to the AQA focus on Congress.

perspectives.label: Democrats argue
perspectives.text: The new majority lets them advance their agenda on climate and health.

perspectives.label: Republicans argue
perspectives.text: Losses reflect voter backlash against current policies.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressives see an opportunity for systemic reforms.

key_term.definition: When one party holds more than half the seats in a legislative chamber.

stories.exam_use: Cite to discuss how party control of Congress influences policy outcomes in a comparative essay.

stories.title: Welsh charities call for polluter taxes at COP31
stories.what_happened: Welsh charities and campaign groups urged the Welsh Government to demand taxes on major polluters at the upcoming COP31 climate summit. They also called for stronger domestic protections.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows the executive’s role in international negotiations and environmental policy, linking to the AQA topic of the Prime Minister and Cabinet.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Taxing polluters will drive greener investment and protect public health.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Taxes could harm Welsh industry competitiveness.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressive groups see it as essential climate justice.

key_term.definition: A levy on companies that emit large amounts of greenhouse gases.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence of executive influence on environmental policy in an essay on the UK Cabinet’s powers.

stories.title: Free school milk scheme in Wales may end
stories.what_happened: The Welsh Government announced that the free school milk programme, running since the 1970s, could be discontinued. The decision follows budget pressures and policy review.
stories.why_it_matters: Highlights how devolved administrations make policy choices affecting citizens, a key point in the AQA study of devolution and public policy.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Ending the scheme saves money for other essential services.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: It removes a vital support for low‑income families.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Labour and community groups view it as an attack on welfare.

key_term.definition: The transfer of powers from the central UK government to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

stories.exam_use: Reference in an essay on how devolved governments balance budgets and social welfare.

stories.title: Community group risks losing former day centre
stories.what_happened: A local community group that took over a former day centre faces lease termination after a prolonged campaign to reopen it. The building remains unused.
stories.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the influence of pressure groups on local decision‑making, linking to the AQA topic of pressure groups and participation.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: The group provides essential services for vulnerable residents.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: The lease termination follows legal and financial obligations.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Activists see it as a failure of public services.

key_term.definition: An organised group that seeks to influence public policy without seeking election.

stories.exam_use: Use as a case study of local pressure group impact in an essay on political participation.

compare.uk: The Welsh Government’s policy review of free school milk shows how devolved elections can shape welfare priorities at a regional level.
compare.us: US midterm elections shifted control of Congress to Democrats, altering national legislative agendas.
compare.insight: Both illustrate how electoral outcomes directly affect policy direction, though the UK example operates within a devolved framework while the US example reflects a federal system.

ideas_lens.text: Welsh charities’ call for polluter taxes reflects ecologism’s emphasis on protecting the environment through systemic change, echoing thinkers like Rachel Carson who argued for regulatory action against pollution.

exam_question.question: Assess the extent to which electoral outcomes influence policy decisions in the US and the UK.
exam_question.tip: Compare the US midterm impact on Congress with the Welsh Government’s policy review after local elections, using specific examples.
